text:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — gpu-pool-exhaustion in cluster-gpu-prod. Queue growth >1200, autoscaler failing to add GPU nodes. Paging oncall (ashley-oncall). Logs attached.
ashley-oncall: ack, investigating. seeing steady queue growth from inference-service. grabbing autoscaler logs and nodegroup state.
ashley-oncall: quick snapshot: pods Pending=430, backoff rate increasing, hotpool at 0/10 ready. autoscaler errors: `AttachRoleFailed` and `LaunchTemplateVersionMismatch` in loop.
mike-infra: fyi I saw taint/label drift after last LT rollout — some nodegroups still use lt-v3 while autoscaler expects lt-v4. could explain launch template mismatch.
ashley-oncall: copying relevant lines from autoscaler:
```
I0319 15:10:12 autoscaler.go:312] ScaleUp: nodegroup gpu-pool-hotspare: want +4, max 8
E0319 15:10:13 awsprovider.go:447] AttachRoleFailed: failed to attach instance profile to node: AccessDenied: iam:PassRole
E0319 15:10:14 awsprovider.go:452] LaunchTemplateError: launch template version 'lt-v4' not found for nodegroup gpu-backfill
```
ashley-oncall: also seeing kubelet taint propagation errors: `taint node operation failed: attachrole not ready` — nodes provision but not JoinReady.
tara-support: customer impact: outbound inference latency for customer acme-corp spiked >30s, some requests 5xx. CS notified ACME and placed on status page.
sam-sre: recommended mitigations: 1) fall back to a permissive nodegroup with older LT we know works, 2) temporarily relax taints to allow burst pods, 3) fix IAM PassRole so new instances can attach profile.
ashley-oncall: applying mitigation step 1: creating nodegroup `gpu-burst-fallback` with launch-template `lt-v3` and instance-profile `redwood-gpu-role-legacy`. will scale to 6.
kevin-ml: can we also scale down some non-critical batch jobs? they are consuming GPU slots. there's a `batch-train` label we can evict.
ashley-oncall: yes, evicting low-priority pods now: `kubectl drain -l app=batch-train --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` on affected nodes.
mike-infra: starting IAM check. looks like a ServiceControl policy rolled last night that removed `iam:PassRole` for the autoscaler role in the prod account. I'm opening a quick PR to restore minimal PassRole permission scoped to `redwood-gpu-role-*`.
inc-bot: incident update automated: severity=high, impact=customers degraded, runbook=gpu-provisioning-fallback.
tara-support: posting update to status page: "We are experiencing degraded inference performance for some customers due to GPU capacity provisioning issues. Engineering is actively mitigating."
ashley-oncall: gpu-burst-fallback up: 6 nodes, kubejoin succeeded for 4, 2 pending with `AttachRoleFailed`. starting to Cordon+untaint nodes that joined to accept pods: `kubectl taint nodes node-... gpu:NoSchedule-`
sam-sre: good, queue dropping from 1200 -> 600. still seeing ~150 Pending.
mike-infra: IAM PR merged. giving autoscaler and instance role a small window to retry. triggering nodegroup refresh for gpu-backfill.
kevin-ml: observed request failures to ACME down from 8% -> 2% after backfill nodes started accepting pods.
ashley-oncall: running post-mitigation checks: perf dashboards show p50 latency improving, token cost stable. will keep autoscaler logs on watch.
customer-ops: ACME notified — they acknowledged and marked as "monitoring".
ashley-oncall: root cause hypothesis: LT rollout + IAM policy change caused a subset of nodegroups to reference missing LT version and autoscaler lacked PassRole to attach required instance profile -> instances launched but could not become JoinReady due to attach failures and taints not propagating. Hotpool exhausted -> queue growth -> backlog.
sam-sre: action items: 1) reconcile LT versions across nodegroups (mike), 2) audit recent IAM changes and tighten deploy guardrails (mike + infra), 3) add autoscaler retry/backoff for AttachRole errors and better alerting (kevin + runtime), 4) add an emergency fallback nodegroup automation in playbook (ashley).
mike-infra: will rotate launch-template rollout to a canary first and add preflight that checks IAM perms for autoscaler role.
inc-bot: note added to incident log.
ashley-oncall: handing off to mike-infra for follow-up and remediation. oncall handoff: mike-infra takes ownership at 16:20 UTC. I'll remain available for escalation.
mike-infra: taking over. ETA for full remediation (LT reconciliation + replay test): 3h. I'll post progress updates.
tara-support: customer comms: posting interim note: "Mitigation applied, most customers showing improvement. Engineering working on a permanent fix."
ashley-oncall: marking alert as acknowledged, monitoring for 30m then will close pager if queue stabilizes. :thumbsup:
